title: Dedicated Capacity Fit Inspector and Resizing Playbook
creator: Priya Patel
description: Build an automated inspector and prescriptive playbook that analyzes dedicated fleet utilization and recommends safe right-sizing and autoscale parameter changes. The goal is to reduce committed GPU spend while preserving throughput guarantees (P95 latency & P50 token/sec SLAs) and minimizing customer disruptions.
acceptance_criteria: Inspector runs for a given dedicated pool and produces a single recommended target commit (node count) and autoscale delta with rationale
Recommendations include conservative and aggressive options with estimated monthly cost delta and estimated SLA risk
Utilization report surfaced in Console + CSV export and linked to the pool detail page
Automated simulation replays historical traffic to validate recommendation for the last 7, 30 days and reports fallback scenarios
Integration tests validate signal ingestion pipeline and that recommended resizing does not reduce P95 throughput below policy for synthetic workloads
implementation_plan: Instrument serving runtime to add aggregate signals into kafka.topic:fleet-telemetry (if missing already): slot_occupancy, tokens_per_sec, p95_latency, cold_start_rate
ETL job (Airflow) to roll metrics into analytic table and compute 95/99 percentiles and sustained occupancy episodes (window=5m, 1h)
Cost model module that maps GPU types -> hourly cost + preemption risk factor + cooling/slot overhead
Simulation engine: replay sampled requests from archived traces applying queuing model to detect p95 breach under candidate commit sizes
Console UI: pool page widget + downloadable CSV + CTA to open a rollout ticket with chosen recommendation
Alerting: create OpsGenie rule when inspector recommends >20% resize or when recommendations oscillate week-over-week
algorithm_summary: For each pool, compute P95 token throughput and sustained occupancy windows. Generate candidate commit sizes by binary search on node count that keeps simulated P95 latency within SLA + safety_margin. Score candidates by expected monthly cost delta and SLA risk; present Pareto frontier and two recommended flavors: Conservative (safety_margin=1.25) and Opportunistic (safety_margin=1.05).
decisions: Adopt simulation-based validation vs purely heuristic rules — trades compute for higher confidence
Default conservative safety_margin=1.25 for first rollout; expose as tunable per-customer
Use historical 30-day window as default analysis period, with optional 7-day aggressive view
Surface recommendations but require human approval for commit changes for first 2 quarters
tradeoffs: Conservative margins reduce risk of SLA breach but limit near-term cost savings
Running simulation on long trace windows increases compute costs for inspector; mitigated by sampling and Delta checks
Aggressive resizing may cause oscillation for pools with bursty traffic — we will add hysteresis and minimum time between auto-resizes
